title: AI-Agenter-E2026
text:
Docker file for n8n only
version: '3.8'

services:
  n8n:
    image: n8nio/n8n:latest
    container_name: n8n
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "5678:5678"
    volumes:
      - n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n

volumes:
  n8n_data:
To use this Docker Compose file:

Save the content: Copy the YAML content above and save it into a file named docker-compose.yml in a directory of your choice.
Open your terminal: Navigate to the directory where you saved docker-compose.yml.
Run Docker Compose: Execute the command:
docker compose up -d
Access n8n: Once the container is running (it might take a moment to pull the image the first time), open your web browser and go to http://localhost:5678.

title: 2. Introduction to n8n
text:
The “Recipe” Analogy
A Workflow must be:

Explicit: No guessing. Every step is defined.
Repeatable: If you follow the recipe exactly, you get the same meal every time.
Automatable: Once the recipe is clear, a “robot chef” (n8n) can do the cooking for you.
Programming: Think of it as traditional programming (vs. generative AI)

title: 2. Introduction to n8n
text:
Deterministic vs. Agentic


Deterministic
The Traditional Way

Rules-based: “If This, Then That.”
Fixed Paths: Every step is pre-defined.
Predictable: Given the same input, you always get the same output.
Analogy: A train on tracks.


Agentic
The AI-Powered Way

Goal-based: “Find the answer to X.”
Dynamic Paths: The AI decides which tools to use in real-time.
Flexible: Can handle unexpected data or “fuzzy” logic.
Analogy: A taxi driver.

title: 2. Introduction to n8n
text:
n8n - background


n8n is an open-source, node-based workflow automation tool that enables users to connect various apps and services to automate tasks without extensive coding (No-code/low-code)

Automates complex workflows by connecting APIs, databases, and cloud services.
Offers a visual, drag-and-drop interface to build workflows.
Supports custom code with JavaScript (and Python) for advanced logic.
Integrates with hundreds of applications out-of-the-box.
Useful for automating repetitive tasks, data synchronization, alerts, and more.

title: 2. Introduction to n8n
text:
The n8n Interface


The n8n dashboard is designed to be intuitive and visual.

Workflow Canvas: The main area where you build. It is an infinite digital whiteboard for your logic.
Nodes Panel: Located on the right (opened via the “+” button). This is your library of 400+ integrations and core tools.
Sidebar: Your command center for navigating between your workflow list, credentials, and execution history.
Settings: Accessible via the gear icon in the sidebar for environment variables and owner settings.

title: 2. Introduction to n8n
text:
Core Pillars: Workflows & Nodes


To master n8n, you must understand these three core concepts:

Workflows: A sequence of nodes connected together. A workflow always starts with a Trigger (e.g., a schedule, a webhook, or a manual “chat” prompt).
Nodes: The building blocks. Each node performs one specific action (e.g., “Send an Email,” “Ask ChatGPT,” or “Update Google Sheet”).
Parameters: The configuration inside a node (e.g., which email address to send to).

title: 2. Introduction to n8n
text:
JSON vs. Binary Data
I n8n arbejder vi primært med to datatyper:

JSON (Struktureret data):

Tekst, tal, lister og objekter.
Det du ser i tabeller og “Schema”-visning.
Bruges til logik, filtre og API-kald.

Binary (Filer):

Billeder, PDF’er, Excel-filer, lyd.
Kan ikke læses direkte som tekst af n8n’s standard-logik.
Kræver specifikke nodes (f.eks. “Extract from File”) for at blive transformeret til JSON.

title: 2. Introduction to n8n
text:
Credentials & Executions


Credentials

This is where you securely store API keys and logins (e.g., OpenAI API Key).
Security: Credentials are encrypted and are separate from the workflow itself, allowing you to share workflows without sharing your keys.

Executions

The “Log Book” of your automation.
Shows exactly what data passed through every node.
Essential for debugging: if a workflow fails, you can see exactly where and why.

title: 2. Introduction to n8n

Right-Click & Drag: Move around the canvas quickly.
Mouse Wheel: Zoom in and out.
CMD/CTRL + C / V: You can copy-paste nodes. Interestingly, you can paste n8n nodes as JSON text into Slack/Teams/Email, and others can paste them back into their canvas!
Search (/): Use the search bar in the Nodes panel to find integrations quickly.
Execute Workflow: Use the big orange button at the bottom to test your logic in real-time.

title: 2. Introduction to n8n
text:
Node Types & Categories


🛠️ The Building Blocks

Action in an app: The “Hands.” Connect to 400+ apps like Slack, Google Sheets, or Notion to send or retrieve data.
Data Transformation: The “Filter.” Change data formats, rename fields, or filter out specific information.
Flow: The “Logic.” Create branches (If/Else), merge data streams, or loop through lists of items.
Core: The “Power Tools.” Write custom JavaScript/Python, make raw HTTP requests, or use Webhooks.

title: 2. Introduction to n8n
text:
Node Types & Categories


🛠️ The Building Blocks

AI: The “Brain.” Build autonomous agents, use chains, or search through your documents using vector stores.
Human in the Loop: The “Pause Button.” Stop the workflow and wait for a human to click “Approve” or enter data before continuing.

title: Welcome to AI-Agenter-E2026
text:
Course Overview
This course is an introduction to AI agents and practical automation. You will learn to build workflows that automate real work, to design and instruct AI agents that use tools to complete tasks, and to ground those agents in your own data using vector and graph retrieval.
We use n8n as the workflow platform throughout, so you can see what your agents are actually doing. Along the way we cover large language models and how to choose between them, prompt and context engineering, coding agents, MCP for connecting agents to external tools, and how to test, evaluate and secure a system before you let it act on your behalf.
The course is built around two projects: a two-week project in the middle of the semester, and a final project that you present at the oral exam.

title: Welcome to AI-Agenter-E2026
text:
What you need
You will benefit from having access to one AI assistant of your own choice — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok or another. You do not need more than one, and no assignment depends on a particular vendor.
In the first session we install Ollama, which runs a language model locally on your own machine. It is free, needs no API key, and every exercise in the course can fall back to it — so nobody is blocked by which subscription they happen to have. However, an old or not strong machine will only get you so far, because AI models require large amount of compute.

title: About the course
text:
Studieordningen
FORMÅL OG LÆRINGSMÅL

AI Agenter er avanceret AI, som selvstændigt finder strategi og løsning på komplekse opgaver. LLMer (som ChatGTP) er AI som mennesker kan chatte med og få svar, mens en AI Agent selvstændigt udfører opgaver. En AI agent har adgang til systemer og værktøjer, som den bruger til at udføre opgaver automatisk.​ ​
På kurset lærer du at opsætte workflows til automatisering af opgaver, som spænder fra at få daglige nyheder om f.eks. AI agenter, til et større SOME marketings setup. Du vil lære om hvordan large language models (som ChatGPT) virker og at bruge dem til AI agenter. Du vil lære prompt engineering til instruere AI agenterne til at udføre deres opgaver. Derudover kigger vi på RAGs, hvor AI får information fra vector databaser til deres opgaver​
Vi bruger workflow værktøjet n8n til at sætte vores agenter og workflows op. Der vil være behov en smule JavaScript, hvor det meste dog kan fås fra diverse LLMer uden de store problemer. Der vil være mulighed for at bruge Python e.lign programmeringssprog i det afsluttende projekt, men det er ikke et krav.

title: Week 1: Introduction and setup

Tasks

Task 1: Ollama

Install Ollama and pull the model shown in class
Ask it something from the terminal and check you get an answer
Note roughly how fast it responds - we come back to this in week 4



Task 2: n8n installation

Install n8n on your computer
Check it is working
Check that your data/workflows are stored (you can save and load them - they survive restarts of n8n)



Task 3: Your first workflow

Create: Start a new empty workflow in n8n.
Import: Copy the JSON code from ItsLearning and paste it directly onto your n8n canvas (Ctrl+V / Cmd+V).
Run: Click the “Execute Workflow” button.
Explore: Can you find several different ways to trigger a run?
Verify: Check that it works!

Hint: Look in the Executions/Logs to see the data flow.




Task 4: Create your own workflow

Create a new workflow that does something useful to you
Ideas:

Send yourself a notification (email, slack, desktop)
Fetch data from an API (e.g., weather, news)
Process data (e.g., filter, transform)
Automate a task you do often

Test and run your workflow to ensure it works as expected



Task 5: Create a sub workflow

Create a workflow that is started by another workflow (trigger by other workflow node)
Use the “call another n8n workflow” node to call it
Look at executions in n8n and see that both workflows have been run



Extras

Debug: Can you find the error if something goes wrong?
Expand: Add new nodes to the workflow or start a new one for your “Pet Project.”

text:
Studieordningen
FORMÅL OG LÆRINGSMÅL I
AI Agenter er avanceret AI, som selvstændigt finder strategi og løsning på komplekse opgaver. LLMer (som ChatGPT) er AI som mennesker kan chatte med og få svar, mens en AI Agent selvstændigt udfører opgaver. En AI agent har adgang til systemer og værktøjer, som den bruger til at udføre opgaver automatisk.​ ​
På kurset lærer du at opsætte workflows til automatisering af opgaver, som spænder fra at få daglige nyheder om f.eks. AI agenter, til et større SOME marketings setup. Du vil lære om hvordan large language models (som ChatGPT) virker og at bruge dem til AI agenter. Du vil lære prompt engineering til instruere AI agenterne til at udføre deres opgaver. Derudover kigger vi på RAGs, hvor AI får information fra vector databaser til deres opgaver​

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
Large Language model

An LLM is a type of Artificial Intelligence trained on vast amounts of text data to understand, generate, and manipulate human language.
To break it down:

Large: Refers to the scale of the training data (petabytes of text) and the complexity of the model (billions of “parameters”).
Language: It is built to process communication—not just English or Danish, but also computer code and mathematical logic. Model: It is a complex mathematical representation of patterns found in human thought and speech.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
LLM
An LLM is a highly advanced statistical autocomplete. It doesn’t ‘know’ facts like a person does; instead, it predicts the next most likely word (token) in a sequence based on everything it has ever read.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
What is an AI Agent?


The harness Concept

We place a software layer around the LLM.
LLM = The Brain.
Software = The Body.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
What is an AI Agent?


Key Capabilities:

Reasoning: Planning steps to a goal.
Memory: Remembering past context.
Tools: Interacting with APIs/Databases.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
Example: The Meeting Booking Agent
The Goal: “Schedule a 30-minute sync with Peter next Tuesday afternoon.”


Chatbot (Passive)

User: “Book a meeting with Peter.”
Bot: “Tells you to look up in the calendars and send invite to Peter.”
Result: User has to do the work.


AI Agent (Active)

User: “Book a meeting with Peter.”
Agent: Searches contacts for Peter, checks your calendar, emails Peter options, and creates the invite.
Result: Task Completed.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
How the Agent Thinks
When you give the command, the Agent enters a Thought-Action-Observation loop:

Thought: I need to find Peter’s email address.

Action: Search CRM/Contacts tool for “Peter.”
Observation: Found peter@company.com.

Thought: I need to find free slots on Tuesday afternoon.

Action: Check Google Calendar for Tuesday between 13:00 and 17:00.
Observation: User is free at 14:00 and 15:30.

Thought: I will propose these times to Peter via email.

Action: Send email to Peter via Gmail tool.
Observation: Email sent successfully.

Final Response: “I’ve reached out to Peter with two options for Tuesday afternoon.”

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
The Agent’s “Hands” (Tools)
To book that meeting, the Agent was connected to these n8n nodes:

Google Contacts: To find the right person.
Google Calendar: To read availability and write the event.
Gmail / Outlook: To communicate with the external party.
LLM (The Brain): To decide which tool to use and what to write.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
LLM vs. AI Agent








Feature
LLM (The Brain)
AI Agent (The Worker)




Core Capability
Text generation & knowledge
Goal-oriented task completion


Decision-Making
None (predicts next word)
Yes (chooses what to do next)


Tool Use
No (Static)
Yes (Uses APIs, Web, n8n)


Workflow
Single-step (Prompt -> Result)
Multi-step (Loop until finished)


Scope
Generates language
Performs real-world actions


Example
Writing a poem
Researching a lead and sending an email

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
The “Recipe” Analogy

The Business Process: “Making Dinner for 10 People” (The high-level goal).
The Workflow: “The Recipe for Lasagna” (The specific, repeatable steps).

A Workflow must be: - Explicit: No guessing. Every step is defined. - Repeatable: If you follow the recipe exactly, you get the same meal every time. - Automatable: Once the recipe is clear, a “robot chef” (n8n) can do the cooking for you.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
Agents need workflows

An LLM (Agent) might know how to write an email, but it doesn’t know when to send it, where to get the email address, or how to log the activity in a database.
The Workflow is the skeleton that gives the Agent a purpose and access to the real world.
We don’t just build AI Agents to have a conversation. We build Workflows to give those Agents a job to do.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
Deterministic vs. Agentic Workflows


Deterministic
The Traditional Way - Rules-based: “If This, Then That.” - Fixed Paths: Every step is pre-defined. - Predictable: Given the same input, you always get the same output. - Analogy: A train on tracks.

Agentic
The AI-Powered Way - Goal-based: “Find the answer to X.” - Dynamic Paths: The AI decides which tools to use in real-time. - Flexible: Can handle unexpected data or “fuzzy” logic. - Analogy: A taxi driver.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
The n8n “Superpower”


We build deterministic workflows that use AI Agents as “intelligent stops” along the way.

n8n

n8n is an open-source, node-based workflow automation tool that enables users to connect various apps and services to automate tasks without extensive coding (No-code/low-code).

Automates complex workflows by connecting APIs, databases, and cloud services.
Offers a visual, drag-and-drop interface to build workflows.

Self-hostable, providing data privacy and control.
Integrates with hundreds of applications out-of-the-box.
Useful for automating repetitive tasks, data synchronization, and alerts.
Note: Everything we build in n8n can also be done in Python, for example.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
How to Install n8n Locally
You have two main paths to run n8n on your own computer. Both are free and private.


Option A: Docker (Recommended)

Pros: Isolated environment, easy to backup, professional standard.
Cons: Requires installing Docker Desktop first.


Option B: npx / npm

Pros: Instant start if you already have Node.js.
Cons: Brittle; if you close the terminal, n8n stops. Harder to manage long-term.

If you don’t want to use Docker, you can run n8n directly using Node.js.

Keep it open: Do not close this terminal window while working, or n8n will stop.
Access: Open http://localhost:5678.

Note: Your data is saved in your user home folder under /.n8n. {.fragment}

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
Running n8n (Mac & Linux)
Copy and paste this command into your terminal to run n8n in the background:
docker run -d \
  --name n8n \
  -p 5678:5678 \
  -v ~/.n8n:/home/node/.n8n \
  n8nio/n8n






Note


The -v ~/.n8n:/home/node/.n8n part ensures your workflows are saved in your user’s home folder.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
Running n8n (Windows PowerShell)
docker run -d `
  --name n8n `
  -p 5678:5678 `
  -v ${env:USERPROFILE}\.n8n:/home/node/.n8n `
  n8nio/n8n

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
Why these specific flags?

-d (Detached): Runs the container in the background. You can close your terminal and n8n will keep running.
--name n8n: Gives the container a friendly name so you don’t have to remember a random ID.
-p 5678:5678: Maps the internal n8n port to your computer’s port.
-v (Volume): The most important part. This links a folder on your computer to n8n. Without this, your work vanishes when the container stops.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:

Access: http://localhost:5678
Stop: docker stop n8n
Start: docker start n8n
Update:

docker stop n8n && docker rm n8n
Run the “docker run” command again.

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
Don’t Let Your Workflows Disappear!

Volume Mapping keeps your workflows stored on your physical hard drive instead of inside the temporary Docker container.
Without the -v flag: All your work is deleted every time the container is stopped or updated.
How it works: Your local folder is “linked” to /home/node/.n8n inside the container in real-time.







Data Safety


Think of the Docker container like a hotel room: if you don’t put your things in the “Safe” (the Volume), the maid (Docker) will clear everything out when you check out!

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
text:
Verify Your Setup
To ensure your data is actually saving to your hard drive, perform this “Stress Test”:

Create a simple “Hello World” workflow in n8n and save it.
Stop the engine in your terminal:
docker stop n8n
Check: Refresh http://localhost:5678. The site should be unreachable.
Restart:
docker start n8n
Confirm: Refresh the browser. Is your workflow still there?

Where is my data?

Windows: C:\Users\<your-name>\.n8n
Mac/Linux: ~/.n8n







Backup Tip


Copy this folder to a USB stick or cloud drive occasionally. It contains all your workflows and credentials!

title: 1. AI agenter og automatisering
section: n8n: Where to find your data
text:
n8n: Where to find your data

Windows: C:\Users\<YourUsername>\.n8n
macOS/Linux: ~/.n8n
(Full path: /Users/<YourUsername>/.n8n or /home/<YourUsername>/.n8n)

The Most Important File

database.sqlite

This single file contains all your workflows, credentials, and settings.
If you lose this file, you lose your work.
Back it up!








Finding Hidden Folders


Folders starting with a dot (like .n8n) are often hidden by default. - Mac: Press Cmd + Shift + . in Finder to show hidden files. - Windows: Enable “Hidden items” under the View tab in File Explorer.
